earlier_scan.note: Cant/ludling built on Ikwerre (tonal); the one description exists but is not online; Wikipedia summary covers t-insertion + epenthesis, no stress statement.

sources.note: Summarises Akinlabi & Ndimele only (t-insertion, epenthetic vowel matching in ATR/backness/nasality/tone); no stress statement. Its single reference supplied the archived PDF URL.

sources.citation: Akinlabi, Akinbiyi & Ozo-Mekuri Ndimele. 2012. Agbirigba: The birth of an Igboid language. In Harrison Adeniyi (ed.), New Horizons in Nigerian Languages: Essays in Honour of Professor Ben Elugbe. Saarbruecken: LAP. [read as the author preprint PDF from Akinlabi's Rutgers page, dated 2010-10-21, 12 pp., via the Internet Archive]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is entirely phonological (segment inventory from Clements & Osu 2005, t-epenthesis before every CV syllable, high-vowel epenthesis, sec. 5.3 tone copying and contour-tone mapping onto the epenthetic tV syllable). Tone is the only suprasegmental described; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur (a full-text search for stress/accent the text layer: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Clements, G. N. & Sylvester Osu. 2005. Nasal harmony in Ikwere, a language with no phonemic nasal consonants. JALL 26(2): 165-200.

sources.note: Fullest phonological description of the base variety (Ogbakiri Ikwere, ikwe1241); if any statement about stress/accent vs. tone exists for the source language of the cant it would be here. Applies to Ikwere, not Agbirigba per se.
